what_its_for: Dalteparin is a blood thinner (anticoagulant) that helps prevent and treat dangerous blood clots. It is used to prevent blood clots in the legs or lungs (deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism), especially after surgery or in patients who cannot move around much. It is also used to reduce the risk of serious heart problems in people with certain types of chest pain or heart attacks, and to treat blood clots in cancer patients.
how_to_take: Dalteparin is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), not into a vein or muscle. You will inject it into the fatty layer of skin on your belly (abdomen), upper thigh, or upper arm. Each time you inject, choose a different spot to avoid soreness or bruising. Pinch a fold of skin, insert the needle at a 45 to 90 degree angle, push the plunger slowly, and then remove the needle. Do not rub the injection site after giving the shot. Your doctor, nurse, or pharmacist will show you exactly how to give yourself this injection before you do it on your own. Always use a new pre-filled syringe for each dose and dispose of used needles safely in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
dosing: Your dose is determined by your doctor based on your weight, kidney function, and the condition being treated. Doses are measured in International Units (IU). Common adult doses range from 2,500 to 18,000 IU once or twice daily depending on your situation. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not inject two doses at the same time or on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist right away.
storage: Store dalteparin at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from direct light, heat, and moisture. Do not freeze it. Keep all medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use the syringe if the liquid looks cloudy, discolored, or contains visible particles. Dispose of used syringes and needles in an approved sharps container — never in regular household trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid activities that could cause cuts, bruises, or injuries, such as contact sports or rough activities. Use a soft-bristled toothbrush and an electric razor instead of a regular razor to lower your risk of bleeding. Avoid taking aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), or other NSAIDs unless your doctor specifically tells you it is safe, as these medicines can increase your risk of bleeding. Avoid alcohol in large amounts. Tell all your healthcare providers, including dentists, that you are taking dalteparin before any procedure or surgery.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room immediately if you notice: unusual or heavy bleeding such as bleeding gums, nosebleeds that will not stop, or blood in your urine or stools; coughing or vomiting blood; severe bruising or a bruise that keeps growing; heavy menstrual bleeding; severe headache, dizziness, or sudden weakness; numbness or tingling (especially if you had a spinal procedure); chest pain or difficulty breathing; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or pain, redness, or hard lumps at injection sites that do not go away.
when_it_works: Dalteparin starts working to thin your blood within 1 to 2 hours after your first injection. It works continuously as long as you keep taking it as directed. You may not feel any different while taking it, but that does not mean it is not working. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel fine.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Dalteparin may be used during pregnancy when necessary, but the dosing may need to be adjusted. It does not cross the placenta in significant amounts. Breastfeeding: Small amounts may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients (over 65): Older adults may have a higher risk of bleeding and may need closer monitoring. Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, the medicine can build up in your body and increase bleeding risk. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more frequently. Children: Dalteparin can be used in children, but dosing is carefully calculated by weight and must be supervised by a doctor.
